title: Professional development and career pathways
blurb: Plan CPD that meets revalidation, reflect and use feedback well, and map the career routes open to a midwife in practice, management, education, research and policy.
question: A midwife has completed 35 hours of CPD for revalidation, but 15 of them were online modules she did alone. What else does she need before she can revalidate?

teach.body: SPM 5.18 asks midwives to commit to developing, to understand career pathways in practice, management, leadership, education, research and policy, and to take responsibility for ongoing education. SPM 1.27 asks for continuous self-reflection and seeking and responding to feedback. Code 22.3 requires you to keep your knowledge and skills up to date. In plain English: qualifying is the start. You keep learning, reflect on what you do, and choose where you want to grow.

teach.caption: Plus 450 practice hours, a reflective discussion with an NMC registrant, health and character declaration, indemnity and confirmation.

rows.label: Definition
values: Learning with one or more other professionals

rows.label: Examples
values: MDT skills drill, study day, webinar with discussion

teach.caption: Every CPD record notes method, topic, link to practice, dates, hours, the relevant part of the Code and evidence.

steps.label: Topic and link
steps.sub: How it relates to your practice

teach.body: Five pieces of practice-related feedback can come from any source: women, families, colleagues, students, appraisals, audits, written or verbal. Five written reflective accounts, on the NMC form, each relate to CPD, feedback or an event and to the Code; they need not be long or academic, and must not identify anyone. A structured model, such as Gibbs' cycle, helps move from what happened to what you will change.

teach.caption: NICE NG4 names specialist, consultant and practice development midwives within local skill mix.

teach.h: Support for growth: preceptorship and A-EQUIP
teach.body: Preceptorship is a period when newly qualified midwives are supported by a preceptor. NICE NG4 expects staffing to allow time for CPD, mandatory training, supervision, preceptorship and supporting students. A-EQUIP's formative function, education and development, uses guided reflection and can inform appraisal, revalidation and leadership development. Midwives who want to become Professional Midwifery Advocates complete a PMA preparation programme.
teach.cite: NICE NG4 1.1.20 and terms; A-EQUIP (NHS England 2017)

teach.h: Scenario: Noor plans her next three years
teach.body: Noor, two years qualified, wants to become a specialist midwife in perinatal mental health. With her manager at appraisal, she plans a perinatal mental health module, regular multidisciplinary case reviews (participatory CPD), and shadowing the specialist team. She asks women and colleagues for feedback, writes reflective accounts linked to the Code, and meets a PMA to discuss development. Each step counts towards revalidation and her career goal.
teach.cite: SPM 5.18, 1.27; NMC revalidation; A-EQUIP formative function

teach.text: 35 CPD hours is not enough on its own: at least 20 must be participatory, involving other professionals. Reading and solo e-learning count towards the 35, but not the 20.

items: Revalidation every 3 years: 35 hours CPD with at least 20 participatory, 5 feedback, 5 reflective accounts, reflective discussion.
Participatory CPD involves other professionals, in person or virtual.
Feedback from any source; reflections link to the Code and never identify a woman or baby.
Career routes: practice, management, leadership, education, research and policy (SPM 5.18).
Preceptorship supports new midwives; A-EQUIP's formative function supports education and development.

summary: You can now plan CPD that meets revalidation and use feedback and reflection to develop. You can also describe the career pathways open to midwives and the support available, from preceptorship to A-EQUIP.

A.q: How many hours of CPD must a midwife complete over three years for revalidation, and how many must be participatory?
A.why: NMC revalidation: 35 hours of CPD, of which at least 20 must be participatory.

whyNot.1: The participatory minimum is 20 hours, not 10.

A.q: Which activity counts as participatory CPD?
options: Reading a journal article at home
Completing an e-learning module at home
A.why: Participatory CPD involves interaction with one or more other professionals, in person or virtually.

whyNot.2: Watching a recording without interaction is individual CPD.

A.q: A colleague says a midwife's career can only develop in clinical practice. Which other pathway does SPM 5.18 name for midwives?
A.why: SPM 5.18: career pathways that may include practice, management, leadership, education, research and policy.

whyNot.0: Pharmacy is a separate profession, not a midwifery pathway in SPM 5.18.
whyNot.1: Health visiting is a separate specialist public health role, not listed in SPM 5.18.
whyNot.3: Social work is a separate profession, not a midwifery pathway in SPM 5.18.

B.q: A newly qualified midwife starts her first post. What structured support does NICE NG4 describe for this stage?
B.why: NG4: preceptorship is a period when newly qualified midwives are supported by a preceptor.

whyNot.1: Return to practice is for registrants who have been out of practice.
whyNot.2: Revalidation happens every three years, not at the start.
whyNot.3: FtP review is about impairment, not support for new midwives.

B.q: A midwife logs a CPD study day. Which detail must her CPD record include?
options: The total cost of the study day
Its link to her practice and the Code
A certificate issued by the NMC
B.why: The CPD record includes method, topic, link to practice, dates, hours, the relevant part of the Code and evidence.

whyNot.0: Cost is not a revalidation requirement.
whyNot.1: A manager's signature is not required on the CPD record.
whyNot.3: The NMC does not issue CPD certificates.

B.q: A midwife wants to act on SPM 1.27. Which action best fits?
options: Wait for annual appraisal to get feedback
Ask women and colleagues, then reflect
Complete extra online modules at home
B.why: SPM 1.27: take responsibility for continuous self-reflection, seeking and responding to support and feedback; Code 9.2 asks for feedback from a variety of sources.

whyNot.0: Waiting for appraisal is not continuous reflection.
whyNot.3: Solo modules do not involve seeking feedback.

C.q: A midwife has 35 CPD hours: 15 participatory and 20 from reading and solo e-learning. What should she do before revalidating?
options: Complete 20 more hours of any kind
Ask her confirmer to waive the gap
C.why: At least 20 of the 35 hours must be participatory; she has 15, so needs at least 5 more participatory hours.

whyNot.0: The total is met but the participatory minimum is not.
whyNot.2: She needs participatory hours specifically, not any 20 hours.
whyNot.3: A confirmer cannot waive a requirement.

C.q: A midwife wants to become a Professional Midwifery Advocate. What does A-EQUIP require?
options: Ten years' experience as a band 7
Completion of a PMA preparation programme
C.why: A-EQUIP: to undertake the role, a midwife must successfully complete a PMA preparation programme after a selection process.

whyNot.0: No set years at band 7 are required.
whyNot.1: A master's degree is not the stated requirement.
whyNot.3: PMAs are selected for a preparation programme, not elected.

C.q: A midwife is writing one of her reflective accounts based on a thank-you card from a woman. Which approach meets the NMC requirements?
options: Copy the card with the woman's name
Describe the event and link it to the Code
Write about her feelings in detail
Attach a photograph of the woman and baby
C.why: Each reflective account relates to CPD, feedback or an event and to the Code, on the NMC form, without identifying anyone.

whyNot.0: Records must not include identifiable information.
whyNot.2: Reflection needs analysis and learning, not just feelings, and a link to the Code.
whyNot.3: Images identify the woman and baby.

reteach.title: A three-year development plan
reteach.question: How do you build revalidation and career growth together?

blocks.body: Choose a direction (a specialism, management, education, research or policy). Pick CPD that moves you there, making sure at least 20 hours involve other professionals. Collect feedback as you go and write a reflection soon after each learning moment, linked to the Code. Use appraisal and A-EQUIP supervision to review progress.

blocks.text: Solo learning counts towards the 35 hours but not the 20 participatory hours.

explain.body: Five pieces of practice-related feedback over three years, from any source: women, families, colleagues, students, managers, audits; written or verbal, formal or informal; anonymised.

test.q: Which statement about the sources of a midwife's five pieces of revalidation feedback is correct?
options: It must all come from her line manager
It can come from any practice-related source
It must all come from NMC registrants
It must all come from women in her care
test.why: Feedback can come from any source, as long as it relates to her practice, and must not identify anyone.

whyNot.0: The line manager is one possible source, not a required one.
whyNot.2: Feedback is not limited to NMC registrants.
whyNot.3: Women are one possible source, not a required one.

explain.body: The formative function focuses on developing knowledge and skills through education, can use guided reflection, and can inform appraisal, revalidation and leadership development.

test.q: Which A-EQUIP function focuses on education and development and can inform revalidation?
test.why: The formative function covers education and development and can inform appraisal, revalidation and leadership development.

whyNot.0: Restorative focuses on wellbeing and support.
whyNot.1: Normative focuses on monitoring and quality control.
whyNot.2: Personal action for QI focuses on improving care.

explain.body: NG4 1.1.20: midwives should have time for CPD, mandatory training and supervision, for receiving preceptorship, and for training and mentoring students.

test.q: According to NICE NG4, what should midwifery staffing allow time for, besides direct care?
test.why: NG4 1.1.20: ensure midwives have time for CPD, statutory and mandatory training, supervision and supporting students.

whyNot.1: Private practice is outside NHS staffing planning.
whyNot.2: Agency work is not part of establishment planning.
whyNot.3: Personal administration is not listed in NG4.

explain.body: NICE NG4 includes specialist and consultant midwives and practice development midwives in local skill mix, for example specialist bereavement midwives.

test.q: Which role does NICE NG4 give as an example of a specialist midwife?
test.why: NG4 1.2.3 mentions specialist midwives in bereavement roles.

whyNot.0: An obstetric registrar is a doctor.
whyNot.1: Health visitors are a separate profession.
